To convert, as any animal or vegetable matter, into stone or stony substance. A river that petrifies any sort of wood or leaves.
To ride over or across; to ride upon; to trample down. The carter overridden with [i.
To charge or load too heavily; to burden; to oppress; to cloy. Sir W.
Soft or tender by reason of ripeness; having a tender pulp; as, a mellow apple.
For temporary use; -- applied to a temporary contrivance. Jury mast, a temporary mast, in place of one that has been carried away, or broken.

Making, or tending to make, an impression; having power to impress; adapted to excite attention and feeling, to touch the sensibilities, or affect the conscience; as, an impressive discourse; an impressive scene.
To make poor; to reduce to poverty or indigence; as, misfortune and disease impoverish families.
To sink or lay, as in a bed; to deposit in a partly inclosing mass, as of clay or mortar; to cover, as with earth, sand, etc.
To press closely within the arms; to clasp to the bosom; to embrace. "And huggen me in his arms." Shak.
To introduce, or give tidings of, as by a herald; to proclaim; to announce; to foretell; to usher in. Shak.
To flutter; to flap the wings without flying. And flickering on her nest made short essays to sing.
To break up the harmonious progress of; to throw into disorder or confusion; as, the emperor disconcerted the plans of his enemy.
To renounce all claim to deny; ownership of, or responsibility for; to disown; to disavow; to reject. He calls the gods to witness their offense; Disclaims the war, asserts his innocence.

To cease to appear or to be perceived; to pass from view, gradually or suddenly; to vanish; to be no longer seen; as, darkness disappears at the approach of light; a ship disappears as she sails from port.
A coasting vessel of Arabia, East Africa, and the Indian Ocean. It has generally but one mast and a lateen sail.
To bend down; to stoop low; to lie close to the ground with the logs bent, as an animal when waiting for prey, or in fear. Now crouch like a cur.

To contract violently and irregulary, as the muscular parts of an animal body; to shake with irregular spasms, as in excessive laughter, or in agony from grief or pain. With emotions which checked his voice and convulsed his powerful frame.

To make a sudden, sharp noise, or a succesion of such noises, as by striking an object, or by collision of parts; to rattle; to click. We heard Mr.Hodson's whip clacking on the ahoulders of the poor little wretches.
A long carriage, with a calash top, so constructed as to give space for reclining at night, when used on a journey.
To make torpid; to deprive of sensation or sensibility; to stupefy; as, a hand or foot benumbed by cold. The creeping death benumbed her senses first.
The disposition to do good; good will; charitableness; love of mankind, accompanied with a desire to promote their happiness. The wakeful benevolence of the gospel.
To ask; to inquire or inquire of.
To admit a thing as true; to express one's agreement, acquiescence, concurrence, or concession. Who informed the governor .
To put or bring into credit; to invest with credit or authority; to sanction. His censure will .

An optical instrument for forming and examining spectra (as that of solar light, or those produced by flames in which different substances are volatilized), so as to determine, from the position of the spectral lines, the composition of the substance.
The act of renouncing.
The act of illustrating; the act of making clear and distinct; education; also, the state of being illustrated, or of being made clear and distinct.
The act of anticipating, taking up, placing, or considering something beforehand, or before the proper time in natural order. So shall my anticipation prevent your discovery.

Of or pertaining to sex, or the sexes; distinguishing sex; peculiar to the distinction and office of male or female; relating to the distinctive genital organs of the sexes; proceeding from, or based upon, sex; as, sexual characteristics; sexual intercourse, c
Chewing the cud; characterized by chewing again what has been swallowed; of or pertaining to the Ruminantia.
Lower in place, rank, excellence, etc.; less important or valuable; subordinate; underneath; beneath. A thousand inferior and particular propositions.
Next in order after the third; the ordinal of four.
A gun, pistol, or any weapon from a shot is discharged by the force of an explosive substance, as gunpowder.
A material used for dyeing.
Having a temper or disposition to pity; sympathetic; merciful. There never was any heart truly great and generous, that was not also tender and compassionate.
Having power to examine; appointed to examine; as, an examining committee.
Of or pertaining to pepper; having the qualities of pepper; hot; pungent.

An emphasized or reflexive form of the pronoun of the second person; -- used as a subject commonly with you; as, you yourself shall see it; also, alone in the predicate, either in the nominative or objective case; as, you have injured yourself. Of which right
That one of the four cardinal points directly opposite to the north; the region or direction to the right or direction to the right of a person who faces the east.
A country of Europe and Asia. Russia iron, a kind of sheet iron made in Russia, having a lustrous blue-black surface.
Anything brought to a gelatinous condition; a viscous, translucent substance in a condition between liquid and solid; a stiffened solution of gelatin, gum, or the like.
The highest division, or subclass, of gastropod mollusks, including those that have the gills situated anteriorly, or forward of the heart, and the sexes separate.
(a) Any plant of a genus of herbs (Impatiens) having capsules which, if touched when ripe, discharge their seeds. -- See Impatiens.
A kind of hard finish for plasterwork, made of plaster of Paris and marble dust, and capable of taking a high polish.

The act or process of indemnifying, preserving, or securing against loss, damage, or penalty; reimbursement of loss, damage, or penalty; the state of being indemnified. Indemnification is capable of some estimate; dignity has no standard.
A young woman; a girl; a maiden. Shak.
Any one of numerous species of pseudoneoropterous insects belonging to Termes and allied genera; -- called also white ant. See Illust.
A plug introduced into a natural or artificial cavity of the body in order to arrest hemorrhage, or for the application of medicine.

A man employed in a large family, or on a large estate, to manage the domestic concerns, supervise other servants, collect the rents or income, keep accounts, and the like. Worthy to be stewards of rent and land.
A slender stalk or blade in vegetation; as, a spire grass or of wheat. An oak cometh up a little spire.
A woman's under-garment; a shift; a chemise. In her smock, with head and foot all bare.

A square or oblong cloth of wool, cotton, silk, or other textile or netted fabric, used, especially by women, as a loose covering for the neck and shoulders. India shawl, a kind of rich shawl made in India from the wool of the Cashmere goat.
One who records; specifically, a person whose official duty it is to make a record of writings or transactions.
The quality or state of being propense; natural inclination; disposition to do good or evil; bias; bent; tendency. "A propensity to utter blasphemy." Macaulay.
One who commences a personal action or suit to obtain a remedy for an injury to his rights; -- opposed to Ant: defendant.

A contagious disease of fowls, characterized by hoarseness, discharge from the nostrils and eyes, and an accumulation of mucus in the mouth, forming a "scale" on the tongue. By some the term pip is restricted to this last symptom, the disease being called roup

One of a class of auxiliary numbers, devised by John Napier, of Merchiston, Scotland (1550-1617), to abridge arithmetical calculations, by the use of addition and subtraction in place of multiplication and division.
Strong desire; passion. (Archaic.) Some people have a letch for unmasking impostors, or for avenging the wrongs of others.
Having the legs similar in structure; belonging to the Isopoda. -- n.
A good or evil spirit, or demon, supposed by the ancients to preside over a man's destiny in life; a tutelary deity; a supernatural being; a spirit, good or bad. Cf.
A long and narrow corridor, or place for walking; a connecting passageway, as between one room and another; also, a long hole or passage excavated by a boring or burrowing animal.
A medicine serving to mitigate or remove fever. -- a.
A low, sluttish woman. King.
Paste of bread; a soft mass of moistened flour or meal, kneaded or unkneaded, but not yet baked; as, to knead dough.
A young animal, esp. the young of the bear.
A state of profound insensibility from which it is difficult or impossible to rouse a person. See Carus.
The hole or loop in which a button is caught.
One who bows or bends.
The shutting up of a place by troops or ships, with the purpose of preventing ingress or egress, or the reception of supplies; as, the blockade of the ports of an enemy.
A man who takes great care to dress in the latest fashion; a dandy.
The act of abjuring or forswearing; a renunciation upon oath; as, abjuration of the realm, a sworn banishment, an oath taken to leave the country and never to return.
The act of transferring; conveyance; passage; transfer.
A figure by which the conjunction is often repeated, as in the sentence, "We have ships and men and money and stores." Opposed to asyndeton.

The act of reverberating; especially, the act of reflecting light or heat, or reëchoing sound; as, the reverberation of rays from a mirror; the reverberation of rays from a mirror; the reverberation of voices; the reverberation of heat or flame in a furnace.
The act of qualifying, or the condition of being qualified.
The act of expostulating or reasoning with a person in opposition to some impropriety of conduct; remonstrance; earnest and kindly protest; dissuasion. We must use expostulation kindly.
Of or pertaining to India proper; also to the East Indies, or, sometimes, to the West Indies.
One who worships; one who pays divine honors to any being or thing; one who adores. [Written also worshipper.]

The act or process of generalizing; the act of bringing individuals or particulars under a genus or class; deduction of a general principle from particulars. Generalization is only the apprehension of the one in the many.
An instrument for measuring power in watts, -- much used in measuring the energy of an electric current.

Such as is in common use; such as occurs in ordinary practice, or in the ordinary course of events; customary; ordinary; habitual; common. Consultation with oracles was a thing very usual and frequent in their times.
A salt of titanic acid.
The plank, stone, or piece of timber, which lies under a door, especially of a dwelling house, church, temple, or the like; the doorsill; hence, entrance; gate; door.
Strained; drawn close; tight; as, a strict embrace; a strict ligature. Dryden.
One who steers; the helmsman of a vessel. Milton.
Marked with religious rites and pomps; enjoined by, or connected with, religion; sacred. His holy rites and solemn feasts profaned.
Serious in feeeling or manner; sedate; grave; austere; not light, lively, or cheerful. Your looks alter, as your subject does, From kind to fierce, from wanton to severe.
To make known (that which has been concealed or kept secret); to unveil; to disclose; to show. Light was the wound, the prince's care unknown, She might not, would not, yet reveal her own.
Emitting or proceeding as from a center; [U.S.] rays; radiating; radiate.
The act or practice of persecuting; especially, the infliction of loss, pain, or death for adherence to a particular creed or mode of worship. Persecution produces no sincere conviction.
The membrane of fibrous connective tissue which closely invests all bones except at the articular surfaces.
A ternary compound of oxygen and sulphur.
Giving offense; causing displeasure or resentment; displeasing; annoying; as, offensive words.

A story of great but unknown age which originally embodied a belief regarding some fact or phenomenon of experience, and in which often the forces of nature and of the soul are personified; an ancient legend of a god, a hero, the origin of a race, etc.; a wond
A salt of myristic acid.

A loose, flowing upper garment; especially: (a) The ordinary outer dress of a woman; as, a calico or silk gown. (b) The official robe of certain professional men and scholars, as university students and officers, barristers, judges, etc.; hence, the dress of p
An account or history of the descent of a person or family from an ancestor; enumeration of ancestors and their children in the natural order of succession; a pedigree.
An insect that deposits its eggs in plants, and occasions galls, esp. any small hymenopteran of the genus Cynips and allied genera.
Possessing force; characterized by force, efficiency, or energy; powerful; efficacious; impressive; influential. How forcible are right words!
The condition of being festive; social joy or exhilaration of spirits at an entertaintment; joyfulness; gayety. The unrestrained festivity of the rustic youth.
A band of minute tubercles, bearing modified spines, on the shells of spatangoid sea urchins. See Spatangoidea.
The condition of being exact; accuracy; nicety; precision; regularity; as, exactness of jurgement or deportment.
A mineral, commonly of a yellowish green (pistachio) color, occurring granular, massive, columnar, and in monoclinic crystals. It is a silicate of alumina, lime, and oxide of iron, or manganese.
The result of eliminating n variables between n homogeneous equations of any degree; -- called also resultant.
A nonnucleated mass of protoplasm, the supposed simplest form of independent life differing from the amoeba, in which nuclei are present.

A definite summary of what is believed; esp., a summary of the articles of Christian faith; a confession of faith for public use; esp., one which is brief and comprehensive. In the Protestant system the creed is not coördinate with, but always subordinate to,
Covered over; private; hid; secret; disguised. How covert matters may be best disclosed.
A small ruminant of the family Tragulidæ a allied to the musk deer. It inhabits Africa and the East Indies.
A salt of butyric acid.
A rounded mass of anything, esp. a large pill.
The act or process of separating mingled gases of unequal diffusibility by transmission through porous substances.
The letters of a language arranged in the customary order; the series of letters or signs which form the elements of written language.
A crystallizable compound of a salt with alcohol, in which the latter plays a part analogous to that of water of crystallization. Graham.
Without regular form; shapeless; ugly; deformed. Cotton.

A thought prompted by passion or feeling; a state of mind in view of some subject; feeling toward or respecting some person or thing; disposition prompting to action or expression. The word sentiment, agreeably to the use made of it by our best English writers
An overflow; that which overflows; exuberance; copiousness. He was ready to bestow the overflowings of his full mind on anybody who would start a subject.

The passion or emotion excited by the acquisition or expectation of good; pleasurable feelings or emotions caused by success, good fortune, and the like, or by a rational prospect of possessing what we love or desire; gladness; exhilaration of spirits; delight
One who engraves; a person whose business it is to produce engraved work, especially on metal or wood.
A man whose wife is unfaithful; the husband of an adulteress. Shak.
One who checks.

A fortified residence, especially that of a prince or nobleman; a fortress. The house of every one is to him castle and fortress, as well for his defense againts injury and violence, as for his repose.
To play on an instrument of music, or as on an instrument, in an unskillful or noisy way; to thrum; as, to strum a piano.
A vehicle on runners, used for conveying loads over the snow or ice; -- in England called sledge.
Biting; caustic; sarcastic; keen; severe.
Being between the two extremes; middle; interposed; intervening; intermediate. Prior.
The act or using a jig; the act of separating ore with a jigger, or wire-bottomed sieve, which is moved up and down in water. Jigging machine.
Full of faith, or having faith; disposed to believe, especially in the declarations and promises of God. You are not faithful, sir.
Destitute or deprived of inhabitants; deserted; uninhabited; hence, gloomy; as, a desolate isle; a desolate wilderness; a desolate house. I will make Jerusalem .
To put (a vessel) on the other tack by veering her short round on her heel; -- so called from the circumstance of bracing the head yards abox (i. e., sharp aback, on the wind).
Consisting of air; as, an airy substance; the airy parts of bodies.

A person to whom property is legally committed in trust, to be applied either for the benefit of specified individuals, or for public uses; one who is intrusted with property for the benefit of another; also, a person in whose hands the effects of another are
imp. of Shape.
The act of requiring, as of right; a demand or application made as by authority. Specifically: (a) (International Law)
The act or power of perceiving sound; perception of sound; the faculty or sense by which sound is perceived; as, my hearing is good. I have heard of thee by the hearing of the ear.

Forced separation from one's native country; expulsion from one's home by the civil authority; banishment; sometimes, voluntary separation from one's native country. Let them be recalled from their exile.

A tumult; a noisy quarrel; a disturbance; a brawl; contention; discord, either between individuals or in the state. I will own that there is a haughtiness and fierceness in human nature which will which will cause innumerable broils, place men in what situatio
A genus of cycadaceous plants, having the appearance of low palms, but with exogenous wood. See Coontie, and Illust.
A yellow oil having a geraniumlike odor, produced as a side product in making phorone; -- called also xylite oil.
A genus of cetaceans having a long, pointed, bony beak, usually two tusklike teeth in the lower jaw, but no teeth in the upper jaw.
Well-twisted yarn spun of long-staple wool which has been combed to lay the fibers parallel, used for carpets, cloth, hosiery, gloves, and the like.

A genus of minute, pale-green, globular, organisms, about one fiftieth of an inch in diameter, found rolling through water, the motion being produced by minute colorless cilia. It has been considered as belonging to the flagellate Infusoria, but is now referre

A white crystalline aldehyde having a burning taste and characteristic odor of vanilla. It is extracted from vanilla pods, and is also obtained by the decomposition of coniferin, and by the oxidation of eugenol.

A genus of lichens, most of the species of which have long, gray, pendulous, and finely branched fronds. Usnea barbata is the common bearded lichen which grows on branches of trees in northern forests.

Full of use, advantage, or profit; producing, or having power to produce, good; serviceable for any end or object; helpful toward advancing any purpose; beneficial; profitable; advantageous; as, vessels and instruments useful in a family; books useful for impr
An order of amphibians having the tail well developed and often long. It comprises the salamanders, tritons, and allied animals.
An extensive division of Mammalia including those having claws or nails, as distinguished from the hoofed animals (Ungulata).
A stratum of clay lying beneath a coal bed, often containing the roots of coal plants, especially the Stigmaria.
A figure having eleven angles and eleven sides.

To act the tyrant; to exercise arbitrary power; to rule with unjust and oppressive severity; to exercise power others not permitted by law or required by justice, or with a severity not necessary to the ends of justice and government; as, a prince will often t
A stone or fossil which has on it impressions or figures of plants and animals.
The active young larva of any oil beetle. It has feet armed with three claws, and is parasitic on bees.
A genus of fresh-water or river turtles which have the shell imperfectly developed and covered with a soft leathery skin. They are noted for their agility and rapacity.

A genus of epiphytic endogenous plants found in the Southern United States and in tropical America. Tillandsia usneoides, called long moss, black moss, Spanish moss, and Florida moss, has a very slender pendulous branching stem, and forms great hanging tufts o

A genus of evergreen trees, thickly branched, remarkable for the distichous arrangement of their branches, and having scalelike, closely imbricated, or compressed leaves. [Written also thuya.] See Thyine wood.
A division of cirripeds including those which have six thoracic segments, usually bearing six pairs of cirri. The common barnacles are examples.
A group of rocks having a common age or origin; -- nearly equivalent to formation, but used somewhat less comprehensively.
One of a long-established English breed of large pigs. They are red, often spotted with black, with a long snout and erect or forwardly pointed ears, and are valued as bacon producers.

An order of small apterous insects having an elongated body, with three pairs of thoracic and about nine pairs of abdominal legs. They are, in many respects, intermediate between myriapods and true insects.
A genus of meliaceous trees consisting of one species (Sweitenia Mahogoni), the mahogany tree.
An order of Infusoria having the body armed with somewhat stiff, tubular processes which they use as suckers in obtaining their food. They are usually stalked.

A subdivision of a genus, comprising one or more species which differ from other species of the genus in some important character or characters; as, the azaleas now constitute a subgenus of Rhododendron.
A genus of plants related to the banana, found at the Cape of Good Hope. They have rigid glaucous distichous leaves, and peculiar richly colored flowers.
A book containing stories, or short narratives, either true or false.
An extensive group of echinoderms, comprising the starfishes and ophiurans.

An extensive division of marine Annelida, including those that are without oral tentacles or cirri, and have the gills, when present, mostly arranged along the sides of the body. They generally live in burrows or tubes.
A fish having spines in, or in front of, the dorsal fins.
A minute spherical crystalline body having a radiated structure, observed in some vitreous volcanic rocks, as obsidian and pearlstone.
A peculiar sense organ found upon the exterior of most kinds of sea urchins, and consisting of an oval or sherical head surmounting a short pedicel. It is generally supposed to be an olfactory organ.
A division of arachnids having large, powerful fangs and a segmented abdomen; -- called also Solpugidea, and Solpugides.
An extensive order of Porifera, which includes those that have the skeleton composed mainly of siliceous fibers or spicules.
A genus of malvaceous plants common in the tropics. All the species are mucilaginous, and some have tough ligneous fibers which are used as a substitute for hemp and flax.
A genus of shrubs having silvery scurfy leaves, and belonging to the same family as Elæagnus; also, any plant of this genus. See Buffalo berry, under Buffalo.

A combining form (also used adjectively) denoting that three atoms or equivalents of the substance to the name of which it is prefixed are combined with two of some other element or radical; as, sesquibromide, sesquicarbonate, sesquichloride, sesquioxide.
A combining form (also used adjectively) denoting the presence of selenium or its compounds; as, selenio-phosphate, a phosphate having selenium in place of all, or a part, of the oxygen.
A genus of plants, mostly perennial, having succulent leaves and cymose flowers; orpine; stonecrop. Gray.
Of or pertaining to a sundial. Sciotheric telescope (Dialing), an instrument consisting of a horizontal dial, with a telescope attached to it, used for determining the time, whether of day or night.
A comprehensive group of vertebrates, comprising the reptiles and birds.
A variety of onyx consisting of sard and white chalcedony in alternate layers.
A fruit consisting of many dry indehiscent cells, which contain but few seeds and cohere about a common style, as in the mallows.
An acute specific disease with a dusky red cutaneous eruption resembling that of measles, but unattended by catarrhal symptoms; -- called also German measles.

An extensive class of Protozoa, including those which have pseudopodia, by means of which they move about and take their food. The principal groups are Lobosa (or Amoebea), Helizoa, Radiolaria, and Foraminifera (or Reticularia).
To saw again; specifically, to saw a balk, or a timber, which has already been squared, into dimension lumber, as joists, boards, etc.
A class of air-breathing oviparous vertebrates, usually covered with scales or bony plates. The heart generally has two auricles and one ventricle.
An ornamental foliation having four lobes, or foils.

A division of the Primates comprising the apes and monkeys; -- so called because the hind foot is usually prehensile, and the great toe opposable somewhat like a thumb. Formerly the Quadrumana were considered an order distinct from the Bimana, which last inclu

A phenol metameric with phloroglucin, obtained by the distillation of gallic acid as a poisonous white crystalline substance having acid properties, and hence called also pyrogallic acid. It is a strong reducer, and is used as a developer in photography and in

An apparatus for producing artificial respiration by pumping oxygen or air or a mixture of the two into and out of the lungs, as of a person who has been asphyxiated by drowning, breathing poisonous gases, or the like, or of one who has been stunned by an elec
A division of gastropod mollusks having the teeth of the radula arranged in long transverse rows, somewhat like the barbs of a feather.
A hydrous oxide of manganese, occurring in smooth, botryoidal forms, and massive, and having an iron-black or steel-gray color.
A division of fresh-water rhizopods including those that have a soft body and delicate branched pseudopodia. The genus Gromia is one of the best-known.
A South Africa genus of Carnivora, allied to the hyenas, but smaller and having weaker jaws and teeth. It includes the aard-wolf.
An order of aquatic amphibians having prominent external gills and four legs. It includes Proteus and Menobranchus (Necturus).
A suborder of Gephyræa, having a cylindrical body with a terminal anal opening, and usually with one or two caudal gills.
A species of shark (Lamna cornubica), about eight feet long, having a pointed nose and a crescent-shaped tail; -- called also mackerel shark. [Written also probeagle.]
The condition of having more than two teats, or nipples.
The condition of having more than two mammæ, or breasts.
A solid having many summits or angular points; a polyhedron.
A division of holothurians having an internal gill, or respiratory tree.
A division of Mammalia including those that have a placenta, or all the orders above the marsupials.
A species of wall made of stiff earth or clay rammed in between molds which are carried up as the wall rises; -- called also pisé work. Gwilt.
The free-swimming, hat-shaped larva of certain nemertean worms. It has no resemblance to its parent, and the young worm develops in its interior.

A genus of coniferous trees of the northen hemisphere, including the Norway spruce and the American black and white spruces. These trees have pendent cones, which do not readily fall to pieces, in this and other respects differing from the firs.
An order of Entomostraca including a large number of species, most of which live in fresh water. They have flattened or leaflike legs, often very numerous, which they use in swimming.
An imido derivative of phthalic acid, obtained as a white crystalline substance, C6H4.(CO)2NH, which has itself (like succinimide) acid properties, and forms a series of salts. Cf.
A division of ciliated Infusoria having a circle of cilia around the oral disk and sometimes another around the body. It includes the vorticellas.
A solid having five summits or angular points.
A large genus of plants of the order Geraniaceæ, differing from Geranium in having a spurred calyx and an irregular corolla.
An order of holothurians, including those that have ambulacral suckers, or feet, and an internal gill.

A staff corps in the United States navy, consisting of pay directors, pay inspectors, paymasters, passed assistant paymasters, and assistant paymasters, having relative rank from captain to ensign, respectively.
An order of small myriapods having only nine pairs of legs and destitute of tracheæ.
A genus of trees of the order Scrophulariaceæ, consisting of one species, Paulownia imperialis.
A deep pie or pudding made of baked apples, or of sliced bread and apples baked together, with no bottom crust.

Of or relating to the god Pan. Pandean pipes, a primitive wind instrument, consisting of a series of short hollow reeds or pipes, graduated in length by the musical scale, and fastened together side by side; a syrinx; a mouth organ; -- said to have been invent
A genus of plectognath fishes having the body covered with solid, immovable, bony plates. It includes the trunkfishes.

A fern of the genus Osmunda, or flowering fern. The most remarkable species is the osmund royal, or royal fern (Osmunda regalis), which grows in wet or boggy places, and has large bipinnate fronds, often with a panicle of capsules at the top.
A genus of dark green, or purplish black, filamentous, fresh- water algæ, the threads of which have an automatic swaying or crawling motion. Called also Oscillatoria.
A low plant with fleshy leaves (Sedum telephium), having clusters of purple flowers. It is found on dry, sandy places, and on old walls, in England, and has become naturalized in America.
An order of eellike fishes having the scapular arch attached to the vertebræ, but not connected with the skull.
Consisting of oil; containing oil; having the nature or qualities of oil; unctuous; oleaginous; as, oily matter or substance. Bacon.
An animal having eight feet, as a spider.
An atom or radical which has a valence of eight, or is octavalent.

One of the higher wind instruments in the modern orchestra, yet of great antiquity, having a penetrating pastoral quality of tone, somewhat like the clarinet in form, but more slender, and sounded by means of a double reed; a hautboy. Oboe d'amore Etym: [It.,

A genus of birds allied to the gallinules, but having rudimentary wings and incapable of flight. Notornis Mantelli was first known as a fossil bird of New Zealand, but subsequently a few individuals were found living on the southern island.
A figure or polygon having nine sides and nine angles.
A South American bat of the genus Noctilio, having cheek pouches and large incisor teeth.
A binary compound of nitrogen with a more metallic element or radical; as, boric nitride.

The upright post about which the steps of a circular staircase wind; hence, in stairs having straight flights, the principal post at the foot of a staircase, or the secondary ones at the landings. See Hollow newel, under Hollow.
A cordlike organ composed of elastic fibers situated above the ventral nervous cord of annelids, like the earthworm. -- Neu`ro*cor"dal, a.
An order of worms, having a long, round, and generally smooth body; the roundworms. they are mostly parasites.
Apropriate to the relation of neighbors; having frequent or familiar intercourse; kind; civil; social; friendly. -- adv.
A specied of wild sheep (Ovis Hodgsonii), native of Nepaul and Thibet. It has a dorsal mane and a white ruff beneath the neck.
An order of curious parasitic worms found on crinoids. The body is short and disklike, with four pairs of suckers and five pairs of hook-bearing parapodia on the under side.
A genus of large eels of the family Mirænidæ. They differ from the common eel in lacking pectoral fins and in having the dorsal and anal fins continuous.

Containing more than once, or more than one; consisting of more than one; manifold; repeated many times; having several, or many, parts. Law of multiple proportion (Chem.), the generalization that when the same elements unite in more than one proportion, formi

Of or pertaining to the style of work called mosaic; formed by uniting pieces of different colors; variegated; tessellated; also, composed of various materials or ingredients. A very beautiful mosaic pavement.
To do wrongly. Afford me place to show what recompense To wards thee I intend for what I have misdone.
A genus of leguminous plants, containing many species, and including the sensitive plants (Mimosa sensitiva, and M. pudica).
Possessing might; having great power or authority. Wise in heart, and mighty in strength.
The female of the horse and other equine quadrupeds.
A genus of monkeys, found in Asia and the East Indies. They have short tails and prominent eyebrows.

A genus of Old World plants belonging to the Pink family (Caryophyllaceæ). Most of the species have brilliantly colored flowers and cottony leaves, which may have anciently answered as wicks for lamps.
A genus of small pectinibranch mollusks, having thick spiral shells, abundant between tides on nearly all rocky seacoasts. They feed on seaweeds.
A tumor consisting of fat or adipose tissue. -- Li*pom"a*tous, a.
A mineral of pale steel-gray color and metallic luster, occurring in isometric crystals, and also massive. It is a sulphide of cobalt containing some nickel or copper.
The Hawaiian name for seaweeds. Over sixty kinds are used as food, and have species names, as Limu Lipoa, Limu palawai, etc.
An eel-shaped ganoid fish of the order Dipnoi, having both gills and lungs. It inhabits the rivers of South America.
A species of mica, of a lilac or rose-violet color, containing lithia. It usually occurs in masses consisting of small scales.
A genus of ranunculaceous plants (Delphinium), having showy flowers, and a spurred calyx. They are natives of the North Temperate zone.
A kind of elastic floor cloth, made of India rubber, gutta- percha, linseed oil, and powdered cork.
A genus of chilognathous myriapods. The body is long and round, consisting of numerous smooth, equal segments, each of which bears two pairs of short legs.
A silicate of alumina, iron, and magnesia, having a bright blue color and vitreous luster; cordierite. It is remarkable for its dichroism, and is also called dichroite.

Apt to intrude; characterized by intrusion; entering without right or welcome. Intrusive rocks (Geol.), rocks which have been forced, while in a plastic or melted state, into the cavities or between the cracks or layers of other rocks.
A genus of leguminous plants having many species, mostly in tropical countries, several of them yielding indigo, esp. Indigofera tinctoria, and I.

A compound with, or derivative of, the imido group; specif., a compound of one or more acid radicals with the imido group, or with a monamine; hence, also, a derivative of ammonia, in which two atoms of hydrogen have been replaced by divalent basic or acid rad
A morphological unit, consisting of two or more plastids, which does not possess the positive character of the person or stock, in distinction from the physiological organ or biorgan. See Morphon.

A surface of the second order, which is cut by certain planes in hyperbolas; also, the solid, bounded in part by such a surface. Hyperboloid of revolution, an hyperboloid described by an hyperbola revolving about one of its axes.
An alkaloid associated with cocaine in coca leaves (Erythroxylon coca), and extracted as a thick, yellow oil, having a pungent taste and odor.

A combining form, also used adjectively, indicating hydroxyl as an ingredient. Hydroxy acid (Chem.), an organic acid, having (besides the hydroxyl group of the carboxyl radical) an alcoholic hydroxyl group, and thus having the qualities of an alcohol in additi
A genus of small rubiaceous herbs, having tetramerous salveform blue or white flower. There are about twenty species, natives of North America.
A word having the same sound as another, but differing from it in meaning; as the noun bear and the verb bear. [Written also homonyme.]
Belonging to, or having the characteristics of, home; domestic; familiar; intimate. [Archaic] With all these men I was right homely, and communed with, them long and oft.

An atom which has a valence of seven, and which can be theoretically combined with, substituted for, or replaced by, seven monad atoms or radicals; as, iodine is a heptad in iodic acid. Also used as an adjective.
An order of fresh-water rhizopods having a more or less globular form, with slender radiating pseudopodia; the sun animalcule.
Containing sand or grit; consisting of grit; caused by grit; full of hard particles.
An oyster which has the gills tinged with a green pigment, said to be due to an abnormal condition of the blood.
A comprehensive division of vertebrates, including all that have distinct jaws, in contrast with the leptocardians and marsipobranchs (Cyclostoma), which lack them. [Written also Gnathostomata.]
An apparatus for the generation of gases, or for impregnating a liquid with a gas, or a gas with a volatile liquid.
Full of foam or froth, or consisting of froth or light bubbles; spumous; foamy.
A small beetle of the family Halticidæ, of many species. They have strong posterior legs and leap like fleas.
A genus of fishes, having the head prolonged into a tube, with the mouth at the extremity.
A genus of marine gastropod mollusks, having a conical or limpetlike shell, with an opening at the apex; -- called also keyhole limpet.
A singular marine fish of the genus Pterois, family Scorpænidæ, of several species, inhabiting the Indo-Pacific region. They are usually red, and have very large spinose pectoral and dorsal fins.
The tissue which fills the interspaces between the costæ of many madreporarian corals, usually consisting of small transverse or oblique septa.
A brownish black mineral with a metallic luster, found in Norway. It contains niobium, titanium, yttrium, and uranium, with some other metals.
The fundamental forms of organic life, that are composed of two equal and symmetrical halves. Syd.
A genus of umbelliferous plants somewhat like thistles in appearance. Eryngium maritimum, or sea holly, has been highly esteemed as an aphrodisiac, the roots being formerly candied.
A genus of cactaceous plants having flattened, jointed stems, and petals united in a tube. The flowers are very showy, and several species are in cultivation.
A mineral consisting of both the chloride and the bromide of silver.
A kind of posset made of eggs, brandy, sugar, and ale. Lamb.
A mineral consisting of antimony and silver.
An order of gastropods, including the true limpets, and having the teeth on the odontophore or lingual ribbon.
A compound of a binary type containing two cyanogen groups or radicals; -- called also bicyanide.

A combining form (also used adjectively), meaning pertaining to, or derived from, a series of compounds containing a radical of two nitrogen atoms, united usually to an aromatic radical; as, diazo- benzene, C6H5.N2.OH.

A disease which is attended with a persistent, excessive discharge of urine. Most frequently the urine is not only increased in quantity, but contains saccharine matter, in which case the disease is generally fatal.
The tribe of aquatic Amphibia which includes Amphiuma, Menopoma, etc. They have permanent gill openings, but no external gills; -- called also Cryptobranchiata.
The division of Cephalopoda which includes the squids, cuttlefishes, and others having ten arms or tentacles; -- called also Decapoda. [Written also Decacera.] See Dibranchiata.

A contrivance for producing manifold copies of writing or drawing. The writing or drawing is done with a style carrying a small wheel at the end which makes minute punctures in the paper, thus converting it into a stencil.
A glass of fishes having a suckerlike mouth, without jaws, as the lamprey; the Marsipobranchii.
The bark of a South American vine (Gonolobus Condurango) of the Milkweed family. It has been supposed, but erroneously, to be a cure for cancer.
A genus of plants related to the clover, having their flowers arranged in little heads or tufts resembling coronets.
A genus of herbaceous composite plants, having the achenes two- horned and remotely resembling some insect; tickseed. C.
A large genus of plants having monopetalous flowers, including the common bindweed (C. arwensis), and formerly the morning-glory, but this is now transferred to the genus Ipomæa.
A tribe of perching birds, including those which have a strong conical bill, as the finches.
A large family of dicotyledonous plants, having their flowers arranged in dense heads of many small florets and their anthers united in a tube. The daisy, dandelion, and asters, are examples.
An apple-green variety of chalcedony, colored by nickel. It has a dull flinty luster, and is sometimes used in jewelry.
A genus of flowerless plants, having articulated stems and whorled branches. They flourish in wet places.
A tie consisting of a series of connected iron bars or rods.
A marine fish of the family Chætodontidæ. The chætodonts have broad, compressed bodies, and usually bright colors.

A genus of ganoid fishes, of the order Dipnoi, first known as Mesozoic fossil fishes; but recently two living species have been discovered in Australian rivers. They have lungs so well developed that they can leave the water and breathe in air.
A genus of carnivorous mammals, of the family Canidæ, including the dogs and wolves. Canis major Etym: [L., larger dog], a constellation to the southeast of Orion, containing Sirius or the Dog Star.
(a) A chest to hold ammunition. (b) A four-wheeled carriage for conveying ammunition, consisting of two parts, a body and a limber.

A genus of low herbs (Pinguicula) having simple leaves which secrete from their glandular upper surface a viscid fluid, to which insects adhere, after which the margin infolds and the insects are digested by the plant. The species are found mostly in the North
A fungus (Ustilago foetida) which affects the ear of cereals, filling the grains with a fetid dust; -- also called pepperbrand.
A genus of land snails having an elongated spiral shell, often of large size. The species are numerous ingabundant in tropical America.
A class of Molluscoidea having a symmetrical bivalve shell, often attached by a fleshy peduncle.
A group of beetles having short elytra, as the rove beetles.
To impregnate with a preservative solution of copper sulphate, as timber, railroad ties, etc.
A binary compound of boron with a more positive or basic element or radical; -- formerly called boruret.
High-sounding; inflated; big without meaning; magniloquent; bombastic. [He] evades them with a bombast circumstance, Horribly stuffed with epithets of war.

A species of grass (Poa compressa) with bluish green stems, valuable in thin gravelly soils; wire grass. Kentucky blue grass, a species of grass (Poa pratensis) which has running rootstocks and spreads rapidly.
A tree having the wood or the sap of the color of blood.
A tiny mass of bioplasm, in itself a living unit and having formative power, as a living white blood corpuscle; bioblast.
The condition of having two mammæ or teats.
A large genus of American, mostly tropical, climbing shrubs, having compound leaves and showy somewhat tubular flowers. B.
A compound consisting of two atoms of chlorine with one or more atoms of another element; -- called also dichloride. Bichloride of mercury, mercuric chloride; -- sometimes called corrosive sublimate.
A muscle having two heads or origins; -- applied particularly to a flexor in the arm, and to another in the thigh.
A recess in a room for a bed. Of the three bedrooms, two have fireplaces, and all are of fair size, with windows and bedsite well placed.
The outer wall of the ground story of a building, or of a part of that story, when treated as a distinct substructure. ( See Base, n., 3 (a).) Hence: The rooms of a ground floor, collectively.
An herbaceous plant of the Barberry family (Epimedium alpinum), having leaves that are bitter and said to be sudorific.
A threemasted vessel, having the foremast square-rigged, and the others schooner-rigged. [Spelled also barquentine, barkantine, etc.] See Illust.
A row of balusters topped by a rail, serving as an open parapet, as along the edge of a balcony, terrace, bridge, staircase, or the eaves of a building.
A genus of marine bivalves, having a pearly interior, allied to the pearl oyster; -- so called from a supposed resemblance of the typical species to a bird.

Pertaining to an average or mean; medial; containing a mean proportion; of a mean size, quality, ability, etc.; ordinary; usual; as, an average rate of profit; an average amount of rain; the average Englishman; beings of the average stamp.
Having omens or tokens of a favorable issue; giving promise of success, prosperity, or happiness; predicting good; as, an auspicious beginning. Auspicious union of order and freedom.
A genus of American monkeys with prehensile tails, and having the thumb wanting or rudimentary. See Spider monkey, and Coaita.
A genus of crustaceans, containing the crawfish of fresh-water lobster of Europe, and allied species of western North America. See Crawfish.
The venomous asp. [Chiefly poetic] Shak.

A large class of higher fungi distinguished by septate hyphæ, and by having their spores formed in asci, or spore sacs. It comprises many orders, among which are the yeasts, molds, mildews, truffles, morels, etc.
The use of the bow and arrows in battle, hunting, etc.; the art, practice, or skill of shooting with a bow and arrows.
The male reproductive apparatus in the lower, consisting of a cell or other cavity in which spermatozoids are produced; -- called also spermary. -- An`ther*id"i*al, a.

A division of the Articulata, having the body formed of numerous rings or annular segments, and without jointed legs. The principal subdivisions are the Chætopoda, including the Oligochæta or earthworms and Polychæta or marine worms; and the Hirudinea or leech

A city of Asia Minor (or Anatolia) which has given its name to a goat, a cat, etc. Angora cat (Zoöl.), a variety of the domestic cat with very long and silky hair, generally of the brownish white color.
An animal of the barnacle tribe, of the genus Lepas, having a fleshy stem or peduncle; a goose barnacle. See Cirripedia.
A variety of trap or basaltic rock, containing small cavities, occupied, wholly or in part, by nodules or geodes of different minerals, esp. agates, quartz, calcite, and the zeolites.
A salt formed by the combination of ambreic acid with a base or positive radical.
A provisional name for a plant which has not had its flowers botanically examined, and therefore has not been referred to its proper genus.

A large division of Anthozoa, including those which have simple tentacles and do not form stony corals. Sometimes, in a wider sense, applied to all the Anthozoa, expert the Alcyonaria, whether forming corals or not.
A plant which has no cotyledons, as the dodder and all flowerless plants.
A salt formed by the union of acetic acid with a base or positive radical; as, acetate of lead, acetate of potash.
Having power, capacity, or tendency to absorb or imbibe. E.
A combination of absinthic acid with a base or positive radical.

To move one way and the other with quick turns; to shake to and fro; to move vibratingly; to cause to vibrate, as a part of the body; as, to wag the head. No discerner durst wag his tongue in censure.
To move one way and the other; to reel or stagger; to waver. [A spheroid] is always liable to shift and vacillatefrom one axis to another.
To weave, as cloth, so as to produce the appearance of diagonal lines or ribs on the surface.
To fall forward; to pitch or tumble down. Though castles topple on their warders' heads.
To shut with force and a loud noise; to bang; as, he slammed the door.

To reduce to scoria or slag; specifically, in assaying, to fuse so as to separate the gangue and earthy material, with borax, lead, soda, etc., thus leaving the gold and silver in a lead button; hence, to separate from, or by means of, a slag.
To scratch or cut the skin of; esp. (Med.), to make small incisions in, by means of a lancet or scarificator, so as to draw blood from the smaller vessels without opening a large vein.
To lament; to regret extremely; to grieve for or over. Chaucer.
To fill again after having been diminished or emptied; to stock anew; hence, to fill completely; to cause to abound. Multiply and replenish the earth.
To meet unexpectedly; to encounter.
To join again; to unite after separation.
To make red or somewhat red; to give a red color to.
To haggle about the price of a commodity; to bargain hard. [Prov.
To make perpetual; to cause to endure, or to be continued, indefinitely; to preserve from extinction or oblivion; to eternize. Addison.

To pass through the pores or interstices of; to penetrate and pass through without causing rupture or displacement; -- applied especially to fluids which pass through substances of loose texture; as, water permeates sand. Woodward.
To reach above or beyond in any direction.
To awe exceedingly; to subjugate or restrain by awe or great fear. The king was present in person to overlook the magistrates, and overawe these subjects with the terror of his sword.
To send in or put in; to insert or introduce. Greenhill.
To introduce gently or slowly, as by a winding or narrow passage, or a gentle, persistent movement. The water easily insinuates itself into, and placidly distends, the vessels of vegetables.
To drive close; to press firmly together: to wedge into a place. Woodward.
To cut short like bristles; as, to hog the mane of a horse. Smart.
To murmur or mutter with discontent; to make ill-natured complaints in a low voice and a surly manner. L'Avare, not using half his store, Still grumbles that he has no more.
To warn beforehand; to give previous warning, admonition, information, or notice to; to caution in advance. We were forewarned of your coming.
Public report or rumor. The fame thereof was heard in Pharaoh's house.

To breathe out; to emit from the lungs; to throw out from the mouth or nostrils in the process of respiration; -- opposed to inspire. Anatomy exhibits the lungs in a continual motion of inspiring and expiring air.
To clear from alleged fault or guilt; to prove to be guiltless; to relieve of blame; to acquit. He exculpated himself from being the author of the heroic epistle.
To fill with rage; to provoke to frenzy or madness; to make furious.
One who has been deceived or who is easily deceived; a gull; as, the dupe of a schemer.
To assert positively; to teach magisterially or with bold and undue confidence; to advance with arrogance. The pride of dogmatizing schools.

To extend from a common point in different directions; to tend from one point and recede from each other; to tend to spread apart; to turn aside or deviate (as from a given direction); -- opposed to converge; as, rays of light diverge as they proceed from the
To discourage; to deprive of courage and hope; to depress the spirits of; to deject. Regiments .

To divest of a sacred character or office; to divert from a sacred purpose; to violate the sanctity of; to profane; to put to an unworthy use; -- the opposite of consecrate. The [Russian] clergy can not suffer corporal punishment without being previously desec
To separate, select, or pick out; to choose and gather or collect; as, to cuil flowers. From his herd he culls, For slaughter, from the fairest of his bulls.

To make matter of controversy; to dispute or oppose by reasoning; to contend against in words or writings; to contest; to debate. Some controverted points had decided according to the sense of the best jurists.
A wood or a collection of trees, shrubs, etc., closely set; as, a ram caught in a thicket. Gen.
The act of protruding or thrusting forward, or beyond the usual limit.
One of the nobility; a noble; a peer; one who enjoys rank above a commoner, either by virtue of birth, by office, or by patent.
That which is meant or intended; intent; purpose; aim; object; as, a mischievous meaning was apparent. If there be any good meaning towards you.

The hard, white, opaque, fine-grained substance constituting the tusks of the elephant. It is a variety of dentine, characterized by the minuteness and close arrangement of the tubes, as also by their double flexure.
In an especial manner; chiefly; particularly; peculiarly; in an uncommon degree.
The act of tasking food; the act of consuming or corroding.
In the first place; principally; preëminently; above; especially. Search through this garden; leave unsearched no nook; But chiefly where those two fair creatures lodge.

Manner of behaving, whether good or bad; mode of conducting one's self; conduct; deportment; carriage; -- used also of inanimate objects; as, the behavior of a ship in a storm; the behavior of the magnetic needle. A gentleman that is very singular in his behav
A large doorway allowing vehicles to drive into or through a building. It is common to have the entrance door open upon the passage of the porte-cochère.

An instrument for viewing the interior of the eye, particularly the retina. Light is thrown into the eye by a mirror (usually concave) and the interior is then examined with or without the aid of a lens.
To utter the ordinary call or cry of a horse; to neigh.
To remove a bolt from; to unfasten; to unbar; to open. "He shall unbolt the gates." Shak.
A small drum, especially a shallow drum with only one skin, played on with the hand, and having bells at the sides; a timbrel.
To sleep; especially, to sleep lightly; to doze. Piers Plowman.
Something scraped off; hence, a small piece; a bit; a fragment; a detached, incomplete portion. I have no materials -- not a scrap.
One who rows with an oar.
To feel resentment. Swift.
To render young again.
To generate and produce; to beget; to engender.
To show, suggest, or announce, by antecedent types and similitudes; to foreshadow. "Whom all the various types prefigured." South.
To pry about; to prowl. [Prov.
Having to do with shipping; of or pertaining to ships or a navy; consisting of ships; as, naval forces, successes, stores, etc.
To deposit, as a dead body, in the earth; to bury; to inter. Weeping they bear the mangled heaps of slain, Inhume the natives in their native plain.
To beget; to engender.
To ordain or appoint beforehand; to preordain; to predestinate; to predetermine. Hooker.
To invest. Latham.
A hard, heavy, and durable wood, which admits of a fine polish or gloss. The usual color is black, but it also occurs red or green.
To free from encumbrance, or from anything which clogs, impedes, or obstructs; to disburden. Owen.
To take or let out the bowels or interior parts of; to eviscerate. Soon after their death, they are disemboweled.
To pay out; to expend; -- usually from a public fund or treasury. The duty of collecting and disbursing his revenues.
To make a low repeated cry or sound, like the characteristic note of pigeons or doves. The stockdove only through the forest cooes, Mournfully hoarse.
Of the same age; existing during the same period of time, especially time long and remote; -- usually followed by with. Silence!
To baptize and give a Christian name to.
Sulphur; See Sulphur.
To deck, ornament, or adorn; to grace. Bedecked with boughs, flowers, and garlands.
To cause obscurity or dimness to; to dim; to cloud. If thou becloud the sunshine of thine eye.
A lubricant or salve for sores, burns, or the like; an ointment. Cowper.

A preparation of vegetables, as lettuce, celery, water cress, onions, etc., usually dressed with salt, vinegar, oil, and spice, and eaten for giving a relish to other food; as, lettuce salad; tomato salad, etc. Leaves eaten raw termed salad.
A string of beads, etc., or any continuous band or chain, worn around the neck as an ornament.

An emphasized form of the third person masculine pronoun; -- used as a subject usually with he; as, he himself will bear the blame; used alone in the predicate, either in the nominative or objective case; as, it is himself who saved himself. But he himself ret
An appellative of Abraham or of one of his descendants, esp. in the line of Jacob; an Israelite; a Jew.
A raised structure (as a square or oblong erection of stone or wood) on which sacrifices are offered or incense burned to a deity. Noah builded an altar unto the Lord.
Being present, or in the train; accompanying; in waiting. From the attendant flotilla rang notes triumph.
Pertaining to, or situated near, the anus; as, the anal fin or glands.
Of or pertaining to the Amphibia; as, amphibian reptiles.
The quality or condition of being a neighbor; the state of being or dwelling near; proximity. Then the prison and the palace were in awful neighborhood.

Producing contraction; stopping bleeding; having the quality of restraining hemorrhage when applied to the bleeding part; astringent. [Written also stiptic.] Styptic weed (Bot.), an American leguminous herb (Cassia occidentalis) closely related to the wild sen
A slow Spanish dance of Saracenic origin, to an air in triple time; also, the air itself. She has brought us the newest saraband from the court of Queen Mab.
Having a decided purpose; determined; resolved; fixed in a determination; hence, bold; firm; steady. Edward is at hand, Ready to fight; therefore be resolute.
Consisting of pus, or matter; partaking of the nature of pus; attended with suppuration; as, purulent inflammation.
A well-known trailing plant (Cucurbita pepo) and its fruit, -- used for cooking and for feeding stock; a pompion. Pumpkin seed.

A prayer; a supplication; an imploration; an entreaty; especially, a request of a solemn or formal kind; a prayer to the Supreme Being, or to a person of superior power, rank, or authority; also, a single clause in such a prayer. A house of prayer and petition
Nearest in place; having no similar object intervening. Chaucer.
A person who lives near another; one whose abode is not far off. Chaucer.
A tough, horny animal substance entering into the composition of the skeleton of sponges, and other invertebrates; -- called also keratode.
Animal fat, as tallow or lard, especially when in a soft state; oily or unctuous matter of any kind.
A half bastion, or that part of a bastion consisting of one face and one flank.
Any great misfortune or cause of misery; -- generally applied to events or disasters which produce extensive evil, either to communities or individuals.
Having the power or quality of acting; causing change; communicating action or motion; acting; -- opposed to Ant: passive, that receives; as, certain active principles; the powers of the mind.
The transference of the relation between one set of objects to another set for the purpose of brief explanation; a compressed simile; e. g., the ship plows the sea.
A suborder of fishes including Gobiesox and allied genera. These fishes have soft-rayed fins, and a ventral sucker supported in front by the pectoral fins.
Having no parallel, or equal; unequaled; unmatched. The unparalleled perseverance of the armies of the United States, under every suffering and discouragement, was little short of a miracle.
A genus of deep-sea alcyonaria consisting of a cluster of large flowerlike polyps situated at the summit of a long, slender stem which stands upright in the mud, supported by a bulbous base.
An extensive artificial group of gastropods comprising all those which have a spiral shell and the foot attached to the base of the neck.

A division of insects, considered by some writers a distinct order, but regarded by others as belonging to the Hemiptera. They are all of small size, and have narrow, broadly fringed wings with rudimentary nervures.
An artificial group of passerine birds having slender bills, as the humming birds.
A division of insects having slender or subulate antennæ. The dragon flies and May flies are examples.

A group of small insects having the anterior wings rudimentary, and in the form of short and slender twisted appendages, while the posterior ones are large and membranous. They are parasitic in the larval state on bees, wasps, and the like; -- called also Rhip
An order of irregular sea urchins, usually having a more or less heart-shaped shell with four or five petal-like ambulacra above. The mouth is edentulous and situated anteriorly, on the under side.

An order of pelagic Hydrozoa including species which form complex free-swimming communities composed of numerous zooids of various kinds, some of which act as floats or as swimming organs, others as feeding or nutritive zooids, and others as reproductive zooid

That which gives a safe, passage; either (a) a convoy or guard to protect a person in an enemy's country or a foreign country, or (b) a writing, pass, or warrant of security, given to a person to enable him to travel with safety. Shak.

A division of marine gastropods having a retractile proboscis and three longitudinal rows of teeth on the radula. It includes many of the large ornamental shells, as the miters, murices, olives, purpuras, volutes, and whelks.
A genus of marine Bryozoa in which the tubular cells have a centralchitinous axis and the tentacles are borne on a bilobed lophophore. It is the type of the order Pterobranchia, or Podostomata
A division of opisthobranchiate mollusks having the branchiæ in a wreath or group around the anal opening, as in the genus Doris.
A cyst or sac of a siphonophore, containing air, and serving as a float, as in Physalia.
An order of fishes generally having the maxillary bone united with the premaxillary, and the articular united with the dentary.

A division of Arachnoidea, including the daddy longlegs or harvestman (Phalangium) and many similar kinds. They have long, slender, many-jointed legs; usually a rounded, segmented abdomen; and chelate jaws.
A dry fruit composed of five carpels, which are covered by an epigynous calyx and separate at maturity.

A plant that affords shelter and food to certain species of ants which live in symbiotic relations with it. Special adaptations for this purpose exist; thus, Acacia spadicigera has large hollows thorns, and species of Cecropia have stem cavities.
An order of wormlike, degraded, parasitic arachnids. They have two pairs of retractile hooks, near the mouth.
The gigantic sugar pine of California and Oregon (Pinus Lambertiana). It has the leaves in fives, and cones a foot long.
A switch consisting of one or more knifelike pieces hinged at one end and making contact near the other with flat gripping springs.
The science of figures having equal perimeters or boundaries.
The act or process of infiltrating, as if water into a porous substance, or of a fluid into the cells of an organ or part of the body.
An order of vitreous sponges, having glassy six-rayed, siliceous spicules; -- called also Hexactinellinæ.
A group of Lacertilia having the tongue forked, including the common lizards. [Written also Fissilingues.]
An outpost consisting of four men, forming one of a single line of posts substituted for the more formal line of sentinels and line of pickets.
Having the quality of preserving from loss, decay, or injury.
A fish of the genus Diodon or the genus Tetraodon, having the power of distending its body by taking air or water into its dilatable esophagus. See Globefish, and Bur fish.
An instrument for pruning trees, consisting of two blades, or a blade and a hook, fixed on the end of a long rod.
A blasting powder or dynamite composed of nitroglycerin, wood fiber, sodium nitrate, and magnesium carbonate.

The art or science of building; especially, the art of building houses, churches, bridges, and other structures, for the purposes of civil life; -- often called civil architecture. Many other architectures besides Gothic.
An animal which has a tongue resembling that of man, as the parrot.
A kind of gun metal, containing copper, zinc, and iron, but no tin.
The act of forming into a class or classes; a distibution into groups, as classes, orders, families, etc., according to some common relations or affinities. Artificial classification.
The quality or state of being thick (in any of the senses of the adjective).
Any animal of the hog kind, especially one of the domestical species. Swine secrete a large amount of subcutaneous fat, which, when extracted, is known as lard.
The state of being sure; certainty; security. Know of a surety, that thy seed shall be a stranger in a land that is not theirs.
An instrument for measuring the direction, duration, and force of earthquakes and like concussions.
The act of saturating, or the state of being saturating; complete penetration or impregnation.
The act of retarding; hindrance; the act of delaying; as, the retardation of the motion of a ship; -- opposed to Ant: acceleration. The retardations of our fluent motion.
The act of restoring anything to its rightful owner, or of making good, or of giving an equivalent for any loss, damage, or injury; indemnification. A restitution of ancient rights unto the crown.
The limit or exterior line encompassing a place; a boundary; a confine; limit of jurisdiction or authority; -- often in the plural; as, the precincts of a state. "The precincts of light." Milton.
A little bite or bit of food. Chaucer.
The state of being man as a human being, or man as distinguished from a child or a woman.
A horizontal member spanning an opening, and carrying the superincumbent weight by means of its strength in resisting crosswise fracture.
The act of bewailing; audible expression of sorrow; wailing; moaning. In Rama was there a voice heard, lamentation and weeping Matt.
Act of pointing out or indicating.

A loose outer garment; especially, a gown forming a part of European modern costume for women and children; also, a coarse hirtlike garment worn by some workmen over their ther clothes; a smock frock; as, a marketman's frock.
A lens of glass to assist the sight. Eyeglasses are used singly or in pairs.
The act of expelling; a driving or forcing out; summary removal from membership, association, etc. The expulsion of the Tarquins.

The sovereign or supreme monarch of an empire; -- a title of dignity superior to that of king; as, the emperor of Germany or of Austria; the emperor or Czar of Russia. Emperor goose (Zoöl.), a large and handsome goose (Philacte canagica), found in Alaska.
That which is eminent or lofty; a high ground or place; a height. Without either eminences or cavities.
The act of ejecting or casting out; discharge; expulsion; evacuation. "Vast ejection of ashes." Eustace.
The act or process of boiling anything in a watery fluid to extract its virtues. In decoction .

A substance, of the consistence of butter or honey, taken from glands in the anal pouch of the civet (Viverra civetta). It is of clear yellowish or brownish color, of a strong, musky odor, offensive when undiluted, but agreeble when a small portion is mixed wi
A dead body, whether of man or beast; a corpse; now commonly the dead body of a beast. He turned to see the carcass of the lion.
Originally, a desk or writing table with drawers for papers. Swift.
One of the subdivisions of the trachea or windpipe; esp. one of the two primary divisions.
A framework for supporting a bed.

Originally, a person put in charge of something especially, a chief officer, magistrate, or keeper, as of a county, town, hundred, or castle; one to whom power Abbott. Lausanne is under the canton of Berne, governed by a bailiff sent every three years from the
The sister of one's father or mother; -- correlative to nephew or niece. Also applied to an uncle's wife.
Act of assorting, or distributing into sorts, kinds, or classes.
A utensil for supporting wood when burning in a fireplace, one being placed on each side; a firedog; as, a pair of andirons.
Along or by the side; side by side with; -- often with of; as, bring the boat alongside; alongside of him; alongside of the tree.
Something actually received; real, as distinct from estimated, receipts. [Cant] The accounts of revenues supplied .
The act of increasing by natural growth; esp. the increase of organic bodies by the internal accession of parts; organic growth.
The act of abandoning, or the state of being abandoned; total desertion; relinquishment. The abandonment of the independence of Europe.

Causing dissatisfaction; unable to give content; unsatisfactory; displeasing. To have reduced the different qualifications in the different States to one uniform rule, would probably have been as dissatisfactory to some of the States, as difficult for the Conv
That swims; capable of swimming; adapted to, or used in, swimming; as, a swimming bird; a swimming motion.
Being or placed within; inner; interior; -- opposed to outward. Milton.
To change into a different form; to transform; to transmute. And earth was metamorphosed into man.
A kind of machine blanket or wrapping material used by calico printers. Ure.
Relating to an angle or to angles; having an angle or angles; forming an angle or corner; sharp-cornered; pointed; as, an angular figure.
To take out of a ship or vessel; as, to unship goods.
To open and shut the eye rapidly; to blink; to wink. The owl fell a moping and twinkling.
To come, or be placed, in the room of; to replace.
To move swiftly; especially, to move as if driven forward by something. The first nautilus that scudded upon the glassy surface of warm primeval oceans.

To repay; in a good sense, to recompense; to return (an equivalent) in good; to reward; in a bad sense, to retaliate; to return (evil) for evil; to punish. He can requite thee; for he knows the charma That call fame on such gentle acts as these.
To print again; to print a second or a new edition of.
To take away; to remove. Multiplication of actions upon the case were rare, formerly, and thereby wager of law ousted.
To blind by covering the eyes. We will blind and hoodwink him.
To twine, twist, or wreathe together or round. [Written also intwine.] Entwined in duskier wreaths her braided locks.
To levy a distress. Upon whom I can distrain for debt.
To become expanded or inflated; to swell. "His heart distends with pride." Milton.
To restrain by force, especially by law or authority; to repress; to curb. Burke.
To hang or attach to, as by a string, so that the thing is suspended; as, a seal appended to a record; the inscription was appended to the column.
Pliant; flexible; easily bent; as, supple joints; supple fingers.
Neat, without elegance or dignity; -- formerly applied to things with a serious meaning; now chiefly applied to persons. "Neat and spruce array." Remedy of Love.

Of or pertaining to the south; situated in, or proceeding from, the south; situated or proceeding toward the south. Southern Cross (Astron.), a constellation of the southern hemisphere containing several bright stars so related in position as to resemble a cro

The uneasiness or pain of mind which is produced by the loss of any good, real or supposed, or by diseappointment in the expectation of good; grief at having suffered or occasioned evil; regret; unhappiness; sadness. Milton.
p. p.
The ground where a military display is held, or where troops are drilled.
Having the quality of producing sleep; tending to produce sleep; soporific.

In law and common usage: A promise to answer for the payment of some debt, or the performance of some duty, in case of the failure of another person, who is, in the first instance, liable to such payment or performance; an engagement which secures or insures a
A glimpse, glance, or gleam. [Scot.] "He saw a glint of light." Ramsay.
A narrow board, thicker at one edge than at the other; -- used for weatherboarding the outside of houses. [U.
Tending, or having power, to raise a blister. -- n.
An instrument for comparing magnetic forces, esp. in the earth's magnetic field.
An insect characterized by having but four perfect legs, as certain of the butterflies.
A kind of ornament consisting of a narrow fillet or band folded, crossed, and interlaced.
Having the power to cure or heal; healing; tending to heal; sanatory. -- San"a*tive*ness, n.

Aërated salt; a white crystalline substance having an alkaline taste and reaction, consisting of sodium bicarbonate (see under Sodium.) It is lagerly used in cooking, with sour milk (lactic acid) or cream of tartar as a substitute for yeast. It is also an ingr
A European wild pigeon (Columba palumbus) having a white crescent on each side of the neck, whence the name. Called also wood pigeon, and cushat.

Any ruminant of the genus Rangifer, of the Deer family, found in the colder parts of both the Eastern and Western hemispheres, and having long irregularly branched antlers, with the brow tines palmate.
To spray (tobacco) with a liquid intended to produce flavor or aroma.
Putting under obligation; disposed to oblige or do favors; hence, helpful; civil; kind. Mons.Strozzi has many curiosities, and is very obliging to a stranger who desires the sight of them.

One who, or that which, has an appetite for human flesh; specifically, one of certain large sharks (esp. Carcharodon Rondeleti); also, a lion or a tiger which has acquired the habit of feeding upon human flesh.

An instrument devised originally for measuring the diameter of the sun; now employed for delicate measurements of the distance and relative direction of two stars too far apart to be easily measured in the field of view of an ordinary telescope.
Smart; spruce; trim; nice. [Obs.
St. Anthony's fire; a febrile disease accompanied with a diffused inflammation of the skin, which, starting usually from a single point, spreads gradually over its surface.
Of or pertaining to the equator; as, equatorial climates; also, pertaining to an equatorial instrument.
The Arabian camel (Camelus dromedarius), having one hump or protuberance on the back, in distinction from the Bactrian camel, which has two humps.
Having or showing good spirits or joy; cheering; cheery; contented; happy; joyful; lively; animated; willing. To entertain a cheerful disposition.
A military headdress or cap, used in the British army. It is of fur, with a bag, of the same color as the facings of the regiment, hanging from the top over the right shoulder.

(a) A square hall lighted from above, into which rooms open at one or more levels. (b) An open court with a porch or gallery around three or more sides; especially at the entrance of a basilica or other church.

Having two or more parts of different curvatures, so combined as to remove spherical aberration; -- said of a lens. Aplanatic focus of a lens (Opt.), the point or focus from which rays diverging pass the lens without spherical aberration.
To talk a weak and silly manner, like one whose faculties are decayed; to prate; to prattle. Stanyhurst.
To pull or draw with great effort; to draw along with continued exertion; to haul along; to tow; as, to tug a loaded cart; to tug a ship into port. There sweat, there strain, tug the laborious oar.

One who has the care of a treasure or treasure or treasury; an officer who receives the public money arising from taxes and duties, or other sources of revenue, takes charge of the same, and disburses it upon orders made by the proper authority; one who has ch

To tease or torment by presenting some good to the view and exciting desire, but continually frustrating the expectations by keeping that good out of reach; to tease; to torment. Thy vain desires, at strife Within themselves, have tantalized thy life.
To unite or knit together confusedly; to interweave or interlock, as threads, so as to make it difficult to unravel the knot; to entangle; to ravel.
To emit a strong, offensive smell; to send out a disgusting odor.

A cutting instrument. Specifically: (a) An instrument consisting of two blades, commonly with bevel edges, connected by a pivot, and working on both sides of the material to be cut, -- used for cutting cloth and other substances.
A long seat with a back, -- made to accommodate several persons at once.
To make or perform a salam. I have salaamed and kowtowed to him.

Anything which resounds; specifically, a vessel in the form of a cylinder open at one end, or a hollow ball of brass with two apertures, so contrived as to greatly intensify a musical tone by its resonance. It is used for the study and analysis of complex soun
To beat to obtuseness; to deprive of keenness; to blunt; to turn back the point of, as a lance used for exercise. But doth rebate and blunt his natural edge.
The product of a second sifting of meal; the finest part of the bran. [Prov.
Final discharge or acquittance, as from debt or obligation; that which silences claims; (Fig.) rest; death. When he himself might his quietus make With a bare bodkin.
A female prince; a woman having sovereign power, or the rank of a prince. Dryden.
A medley or mixture. Specifically: (a) A ragout composed of different sorts of meats, vegetables, etc., cooked together.
A frame of adjustable boards erected on a post, and having holes through which the head and hands of an offender were thrust so as to be exposed in front of it. Shak.
To praise highly; to extol in a public speech; to write or deliver a panegyric upon; to eulogize.
A parchment which has been written upon twice, the first writing having been erased to make place for the second. Longfellow.
A kind of earthen or metal drinking cup, with a handle, -- usually cylindrical and without a lip.
A ring for gauging wooden pins.
To daub; to make dirty; to soil; to defile. Thou ...
A fabled marine creature, typically represented as having the upper part like that of a woman, and the lower like a fish; a sea nymph, sea woman, or woman fish.
A pigment formed by combining some coloring matter, usually by precipitation, with a metallic oxide or earth, esp. with aluminium hydrate; as, madder lake; Florentine lake; yellow lake, etc.
To walk or more slowly; to stay or fall behind; to linger or loiter. "I shall not lag behind." Milton.
To cover with a flood; to overflow; to deluge; to flood; as, the river inundated the town.
To mind; to regard with care; to take notice of; to attend to; to observe. With pleasure Argus the musician heeds.

A musical instrument, resembling a small organ and especially designed for church music, in which the tones are produced by forcing air by means of a bellows so as to cause the vibration of free metallic reeds. It is now made with one or two keyboards, and has
A long, narrow boat with a high prow and stern, used in the canals of Venice. A gondola is usually propelled by one or two oarsmen who stand facing the prow, or by poling.
To flatter; to wheedle; to fawn; to talk smoothly. Chaucer.
A sudden flash; transient luster. LIght as the lightning glimpse they ran.
To hinder; to fend off; to avert; to prevent the approach of; to forbid or prohibit. See Forfend.
To throw or spread out; to flutter; to move ostentatiously; as, a flaunting show. You flaunt about the streets in your new gilt chariot.
A vessel with a narrow mouth, used for holding and conveying liquors. It is generally larger than a bottle, and of leather or stoneware rather than of glass.
To deprive of nerve, force, strength, or courage; to render feeble or impotent; to make effeminate; to impair the moral powers of. A man .
